title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
headline: VBVR-Pro: Scalable, Verifiable Visual Reasoning Suite for Generative Substrate Benchmarking
tldr: VBVR-Pro introduces a scalable framework for native visual reasoning, treating images and videos as problem‑solving substrates rather than mere inputs or outputs. It provides reliable feedback mechanisms and controlled comparisons across generative models, enabling systematic evaluation of visual reasoning capabilities.
significance: By formalizing visual reasoning as a first‑class substrate, VBVR‑Pro unlocks new avenues for AI systems to solve complex tasks directly through visual generation, bridging a critical gap between perception and action.

title: Multicomponent Magnetic Domain Walls in Rhombohedral Graphene
headline: Exploring Multicomponent Magnetic Domain Walls in Rhombohedral Graphene and Their Microscopic Properties
tldr: We investigate a one-dimensional domain wall in valley-imbalanced quarter-filled rhombohedral multilayer graphene, revealing rich spin-valley textures. The study provides microscopic insights into novel magnetic spatial structures that could guide future spintronic applications.
significance: This work uncovers new multicomponent magnetic textures in graphene, opening pathways for valleytronic and spintronic device engineering.

title: Zero-WAM: In-Context World-Action Modeling from Human Videos for Open-Ended Task Generalization
headline: Zero-WAM: Using Human Videos for Zero-Shot Task Generalization in Robotics
tldr: Zero-WAM introduces an in-context learning framework that leverages human demonstration videos to enable robots to perform unseen manipulation tasks without retraining. The method demonstrates strong zero-shot cross-task generalization, showing that task specification alone can drive policy execution.
significance: It shows that large language model style in-context learning can be extended to embodied agents, enabling flexible, zero-shot task execution.

title: RefVideo-6M: A Reliable Reference-Based Dataset for Instructional Video Editing
headline: RefVideo-6M: A Robust Reference-Based Large-Scale Dataset for Instructional Video Editing
tldr: The authors present RefVideo-6M, a 6‑million‑sample dataset that supplies artifact‑free target videos and multimodal instruction signals for video editing tasks. This resource addresses the shortcomings of prior datasets that rely on automatic editing models and limited textual guidance.
significance: By offering high‑quality, reference‑based training data, RefVideo-6M establishes a new benchmark that can accelerate the development of reliable instruction‑driven video editing models.

title: Integrated Hardware Annealing based on Langevin Dynamics for Ising Machines
headline: Hardware Annealing with Langevin Dynamics Accelerates Ising Machine Optimization for Complex Problems
tldr: This study introduces a hardware annealing algorithm based on Langevin dynamics to enhance Ising machines' ability to escape local minima. Experimental results show faster convergence and improved solution quality compared to conventional annealing.
significance: It demonstrates a practical method to overcome energy landscape traps, boosting Ising machines' efficiency for combinatorial optimization.

title: Exact analytical spectrum, eigenstates, and quantum geometry of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model
headline: Exact Spectrum and Quantum Geometry of the Quarter‑Flux Harper‑Hofstadter Four‑Band Model
tldr: We derive closed‑form expressions for the energy spectrum and quantum geometric tensors of a four‑band Harper‑Hofstadter model at quarter flux. These results provide a rare analytical benchmark for topological band theory beyond two‑band systems.
significance: Providing analytical solutions for a four‑band topological model deepens our understanding of quantum geometry and offers a benchmark for future studies.

title: Probing the Properties of Neutral Clouds in the Vicinity of the Local Bubble: Linking three-dimensional Dust with Neutral Hydrogen Absorption
headline: Mapping Tiny-Scale Hydrogen Structures Near the Local Bubble Using 3D Dust and Pulsar Absorption
tldr: Scientists used pulsar observations to detect variations in neutral hydrogen absorption, revealing tiny-scale structures within the Local Bubble. By correlating these variations with 3D dust maps, they uncovered the spatial distribution of interstellar clouds near the bubble’s walls.
significance: This study provides the first direct link between small-scale hydrogen structures and dust distribution, improving our understanding of the Local Bubble’s internal composition.

title: The Isotopic and Elemental Abundances of Planet-Host Star TRAPPIST-1
headline: TRAPPIST-1 Star’s Isotopic Fingerprint Reveals Planet Formation and Galactic Evolution Secrets
tldr: The study measures the elemental and isotopic composition of TRAPPIST-1, a very low-mass star hosting seven Earth-sized planets. These measurements provide insights into the star’s natal material and the processes that shaped its planetary system.
significance: By preserving its natal composition, TRAPPIST-1 offers a unique window into the chemical conditions that gave rise to its compact, habitable-zone planets.

title: Torsion balances as operational probes of semiclassical gravity: Matched-filter bounds, torque-diffusion constraints, and quantum-noise benchmarks
headline: Torsion Balance Experiments Set New Bounds on Semiclassical Gravity via Matched-Filter Analysis
tldr: Using calibrated torsion-balance spectra, researchers derive matched-filter and Cramér-Rao bounds to constrain deterministic and stochastic deviations from Newtonian gravity. The study also establishes torque-diffusion limits and quantum-noise benchmarks, advancing precision tests of semiclassical gravity.
significance: This work tightens experimental limits on quantum gravity effects, guiding future theoretical and experimental research.

title: A Visual Dependence-Aware Framework for Multimodal Unsupervised Continual Post-Training
headline: Enhancing Multimodal LLMs with Visual Dependence-Aware Unsupervised Continual Post-Training for Streaming Data Evolution
tldr: The paper introduces a framework that incorporates token-level visual dependence into unsupervised post-training for multimodal large language models, allowing them to adapt continuously to streaming unlabeled data. This approach outperforms traditional uniform token optimization methods by better leveraging visual context.
significance: It overcomes a critical limitation in current unsupervised post-training, enabling more effective continual learning for multimodal LLMs.

title: MyoMechanix: Biomechanically-Grounded Compositional Skilled Activity Understanding and Coaching
headline: MyoMechanix: Biomechanically Grounded Feedback for Weight-Loaded Actions Using Multimodal Data
tldr: MyoMechanix introduces a multimodal framework that fuses motion capture, muscle dynamics, and physiological signals to assess action quality in weight-loaded tasks. The system provides fine-grained, biomechanically grounded coaching feedback in real time.
significance: It enables precise, personalized training guidance that surpasses visual-only assessments, advancing sports science and rehabilitation.

title: Agentic Autoresearch for Cell-Edge Power Control: Radically Redefining the Researcher's Role
headline: Autonomous AI Agent Designs Wireless Power Control Algorithms, Eliminating Manual ML Engineering
tldr: We show that an AI coding agent can autonomously design and train machine learning models for cell‑edge power control, removing the need for hand‑crafted architecture, loss functions, and training recipes. Using an autoresearch protocol, the agent edits scripts, runs experiments within a fixed budget, and iteratively improves performance.
significance: This work demonstrates a paradigm shift where AI agents take over the entire ML design cycle for wireless resource management, potentially accelerating deployment and reducing human labor.

title: Finding and using interpretable latents in a neutrino foundation model with sparse autoencoders
headline: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Physical Concepts in IceCube Neutrino Foundation Model
tldr: Researchers applied sparse autoencoders to a pretrained IceCube neutrino foundation model, uncovering a validated atlas of physical concepts within its latent space. The method uses strict held‑out tests and nuisance controls, demonstrating mechanistic interpretability for direction reconstruction.
significance: This work provides the first mechanistic interpretability framework for particle‑physics foundation models, enabling transparent, physics‑grounded analysis of complex neural representations.

title: From Producing to Validating: How AI Is Deskilling Freelancers
headline: AI's Rise: How Generative Models Are Deskilling Freelancers in the Gig Economy
tldr: Generative AI promises productivity gains but disproportionately harms freelancers who lack formal upskilling pathways. The resulting deskilling threatens both skill development and job security in the gig economy.
significance: Understanding AI's uneven impact is crucial for designing equitable workforce policies.

title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
headline: Evaluating Action-Conditioned World Models: Do They Truly Follow Robot Actions?
tldr: This study introduces a benchmark to test whether action-conditioned world models accurately simulate futures for arbitrary actions. Findings reveal gaps in action fidelity, prompting alignment techniques to improve policy learning.
significance: Accurate action simulation is critical for safe and efficient robotic policy development, and this work provides the first systematic evaluation and alignment framework.

title: Latent Action as Intention Enables Efficient Future Imagination for World Action Models
headline: Latent Action Intention Boosts World Action Models, Reducing Latency but Hitting Generalization Limits
tldr: World Action Models predict future observations for robot control, yet generating them at test time is slow. Fast-WAM eliminates this step, improving speed but sacrificing generalization, especially with limited data and out-of-distribution cases.
significance: This study highlights the trade-off between real-time efficiency and robustness in future-aware robotic models.

title: What FID Hides: Detecting, Ranking, and Diagnosing Deviations in Generative Evaluation
headline: Uncovering Hidden Flaws in FID: New Methods for Generative Model Evaluation
tldr: The paper shows that Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) can miss significant distributional differences because it only uses first two moments. It proposes alternative diagnostics and ranking strategies that better capture deviations in generative models.
significance: By exposing FID's blind spots, the work guides researchers toward more reliable generative model benchmarks.

title: From Seeing to Acting: Smart Glasses as First-Person Intelligence Platforms
headline: Smart Glasses: From Capture Devices to First-Person Intelligence Platforms Enabling Real-Time Interaction
tldr: Smart glasses are transforming into first-person intelligence platforms that fuse human perception with persistent context and actionable outputs. They must balance power, heat, privacy, and feedback while delivering real-time, context-aware insights.
significance: This evolution unlocks new possibilities for immersive, context-sensitive human-computer interaction across diverse domains.

title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses
headline: Recursive Experiential‑Working Memory Boosts Long‑Horizon Agent Performance by Guiding Skill Selection
tldr: Recuris introduces a recursive Experiential‑Working Memory that tracks task progress and informs skill selection, aligning agent behavior with current needs. This architecture improves long‑horizon task performance by mitigating history‑induced misalignment.
significance: It offers a scalable solution to the recursive self‑improvement challenge in complex, long‑duration tasks.

title: Binary Hypothesis Testing: A Robust Framework Against the Look Elsewhere Effect
headline: Robust Binary Testing Mitigates Look-Elsewhere Effect in Particle Physics Discoveries
tldr: This paper presents a robust binary hypothesis testing framework that accounts for the look‑elsewhere effect, ensuring that discovery claims are not inflated by scanning over parameter space. By distinguishing between pre‑specified and exploratory tests, the method provides a more reliable significance assessment for particle physics experiments.
significance: The framework improves the credibility of 5σ discovery claims by rigorously correcting for multiple testing across the search space.

title: NatPar: Natural Parametric Modeling
headline: NatPar: Parametric Insurance Models for Natural Catastrophes in the Insurance Industry
tldr: We propose NatPar, a parametric insurance framework that replaces indemnity loss adjustments with contractual indices, building on NatCat modeling. The approach aims for practical, industry-standard solutions rather than theoretical optimal contracts.
significance: NatPar offers a scalable, industry-friendly method to monetize natural hazard exposure, bridging the gap between catastrophe modeling and parametric insurance products.

title: SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL
headline: SPO++: Streamlined Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL
tldr: SPO++ removes the need for sibling rollouts by using a persistent prompt-level value estimate, enabling efficient asynchronous RL. The method also demonstrates that trajectory centering improves performance over token-mean actor loss.
significance: This approach accelerates training of agentic RL systems, making them more practical for long, variable tool-use tasks.

title: Fast generation of spectrally-shaped disorder, on the sphere
headline: Rapid Generation of Spectrally-Shaped Disordered Point Patterns on the Sphere
tldr: This work introduces a fast algorithm for creating spectrally-shaped disordered point patterns on spherical domains, enabling efficient exploration of material and computational designs. The method leverages spherical harmonics to enforce Fourier-space constraints while maintaining computational scalability.
significance: It opens new avenues for designing materials and algorithms that require controlled disorder on curved surfaces.

title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
headline: Stable Critic Training for Large Language Models
tldr: We analyze why critic-based RL for LLMs is unstable and propose BPCO, a stable, efficient training recipe. The method allows token-level advantage estimation from a single response, reducing sampling overhead.
significance: This work enables reliable, efficient RL fine-tuning of LLMs without costly multi-response sampling.

title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
headline: ReWorld: Interactive World Model Balances Short-Term Control with Long-Term Memory
tldr: ReWorld introduces an interactive world model that tracks user actions and remembers past scenes in real time. By separating short‑term control and long‑term memory during training and using mixed attention windows, it achieves bounded inference while preserving unbounded memory.
significance: It enables real‑time, long‑horizon interaction for applications like virtual exploration and simulation.

title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?
headline: SWE Refactor Bench: Testing Autonomous Stack Migration with Coding Agents
tldr: The SWE Refactor Bench evaluates whether coding agents can autonomously migrate an entire repository's technology stack, a task beyond current benchmarks that only test functional correctness. This benchmark measures long-horizon, whole-repository changes to assess real-world automation potential.
significance: It bridges the gap between bug-fixing capabilities and large-scale refactoring, offering a realistic test for future AI-driven software maintenance.

title: Physics-Constrained Deep Learning Model for Contactless Blood Pressure Monitoring from Triaxial Bodyseismography
headline: Physics-Constrained Deep Learning for Contactless Blood Pressure Monitoring via Triaxial Bodyseismography
tldr: This study introduces a physics-constrained deep learning framework that extracts blood pressure signals from triaxial bodyseismography data, overcoming variability in body-bed interactions. The model demonstrates robust, real-time BP estimation suitable for long-term, unobtrusive monitoring.
significance: By integrating physical constraints, the model achieves accurate, generalizable blood pressure monitoring without contact, paving the way for continuous health surveillance.

title: Flux-induced Aharonov-Bohm Oscillation in the Tunneling Spectroscopy of Kitaev Spin Liquids
headline: Flux-Induced Aharonov-Bohm Oscillations Reveal Majorana Interference in Kitaev Spin Liquids
tldr: We demonstrate that a single π flux in a Kitaev spin liquid produces an Aharonov-Bohm-like interference pattern in the Majorana continuum, observable via inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy. This provides a direct probe of flux excitations and their mutual statistics with itinerant Majorana fermions.
significance: The work offers a novel spectroscopic fingerprint for detecting emergent gauge fluxes, advancing experimental access to exotic quasiparticles in quantum spin liquids.

title: Quaternionic Hermitian Band Geometry in Four Dimensions: Realization on $S^4$ and Obstruction on $T^4$
headline: Quaternionic Hermitian Band Geometry: Realization on S⁴ and Obstruction on T⁴
tldr: We prove that the minimal‑charge lowest Landau level on the four‑sphere S⁴ provides a global realization of quaternionic Hermitian band geometry, while a saturated, nondegenerate realization induced by a single occupied quaternionic band is topologically obstructed on the four‑torus T⁴. The obstruction arises from an antiunitary symmetry τ satisfying τ²=−1, which forces a nontrivial second Chern class on T⁴.
significance: This work establishes a clear realization–obstruction dichotomy for quaternionic band topology in four dimensions, linking geometric quantization on S⁴ with topological constraints on T⁴.

title: Two-loop renormalisation and Higgs phenomenology in the five-dimensional MSSM
headline: Two-loop 5D MSSM Analysis Illuminates Higgs Mass Generation
tldr: A comprehensive two-loop study of the five-dimensional MSSM shows that power-law running can naturally generate a large stop trilinear coupling. This allows the observed Higgs mass to be reproduced without requiring an excessively heavy supersymmetric spectrum.
significance: It demonstrates that extra-dimensional supersymmetry can reconcile the Higgs mass with a relatively light superpartner spectrum.

title: Provably adaptive sampling with uniform and remasking discrete diffusion models
headline: Adaptive Sampling in Discrete Diffusion Models for Uniform and Remasking
tldr: This paper introduces a provably adaptive sampling scheme for discrete diffusion models that works efficiently under both uniform and remasking forward processes. The authors prove that their sampler achieves near‑optimal complexity, breaking the linear‑dimension lower bound that plagues existing τ‑leaping methods.
significance: It resolves a key bottleneck in diffusion‑based generation, enabling faster, scalable sampling for large‑scale generative tasks.

title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
headline: Prime Agent: Open-Source Harness for Long-Horizon Language Model Agency Evaluation and Workflow
tldr: Prime Agent introduces a persistent IPython REPL that extends recursive language models with external compute, enabling long-horizon evaluation and coding-agent workflows. The open-source harness supports continual learning and real-time reasoning beyond the model’s internal context.
significance: It bridges the gap between sequential language models and real-world agency by providing a modular, testable framework for long-horizon tasks.

title: When "Do Not" Is Not Deny: Security Rules in CLAUDE.md vs Built-In Controls
headline: Do Not vs Deny: Comparing CLAUDE.md Natural Language Rules to Built-In Controls
tldr: We analyze how natural-language 'do not' directives in CLAUDE.md differ from Claude Code's built-in deny controls. Our study of 481 public files shows a measurable gap between the two approaches.
significance: Understanding this gap informs better design of LLM safety mechanisms and policy compliance.

title: FixAnything: 3D-Consistent Rendering Refinement via Video Generative Priors
headline: Refining 3D-Consistent Rendering via Video Generative Priors for Sparse View Artifacts
tldr: This paper introduces a method that uses diffusion-based generative priors to refine 3D rendering across sparse input views, achieving consistent results across representations like Gaussian Splatting and NeRF. By leveraging video generative models, the approach generalizes across different 3D representations without custom architectures.
significance: It offers a unified, architecture-agnostic solution to reduce rendering artifacts in sparse-view 3D scenes, advancing realistic view synthesis.

title: Preparing for the Early eVolution Explorer: The Impact of Flare Temperature on Ozone Column Depth in Earth-Like Atmospheres
headline: Stellar Flare Temperature Variability and Its Effect on Ozone in Earth‑Like Atmospheres
tldr: Atmospheric models often use a 9,000 K flare spectrum, but observations show flare temperatures ranging from 4,000 to 40,000 K. This study simulates how such temperature variations influence ozone column depth over time.
significance: Understanding flare temperature impacts is crucial for assessing exoplanet habitability and atmospheric chemistry.

title: Geospatial & AI Trends: Highlights from 2025 - Geoawesome
headline: 2025 GeoAI Breakthroughs: Predictive Analytics, Automation, and Climate Solutions for Urban and Global Challenges
tldr: The year 2025 saw GeoAI models harness satellite imagery and LLMs to deliver real-time flood detection, crop monitoring, and urban planning insights. These advancements enable cities and policymakers to proactively address climate risks and optimize resource allocation.
significance: These innovations mark a pivotal shift toward data-driven resilience, empowering stakeholders to mitigate environmental threats and enhance sustainable development.

title: Towards the next generation of Geospatial Artificial Intelligence
headline: Charting the Future of Geospatial Artificial Intelligence: Trends, Challenges, and Opportunities
tldr: GeoAI merges geospatial science with AI, rapidly evolving across spatial data science and geography. Understanding recent advances and future directions is essential for leveraging its transformative potential.
significance: This work highlights the critical need to map GeoAI's evolving landscape to guide research and application.

title: Top 5 Geospatial AI Trends to Watch in 2025 - arizton.com
headline: Top 5 GeoAI Trends Shaping 2025: From Foundation Models to Real-Time Flood Detection
tldr: GeoAI is rapidly evolving, with foundation models unlocking new analytical capabilities across satellite imagery and urban planning. Key trends for 2025 include real-time flood detection, precision crop monitoring, and AI-driven change detection in city landscapes.
significance: These trends promise to transform how we monitor and manage Earth's resources, driving smarter decisions in agriculture, urban development, and disaster response.

title: GeoAI and the Next Generation of Geospatial Insights - Geo Week News
headline: GeoAI Revolutionizes Geospatial Analysis: Merging Data, Sensors, and AI for Smarter Insights
tldr: Artificial intelligence is reshaping geospatial science by integrating diverse data sources and advanced analytics. GeoAI empowers organizations to capture, analyze, and act on spatial information faster and more accurately than ever before.
significance: GeoAI unlocks unprecedented precision and speed in mapping, monitoring, and decision-making across sectors.

title: Remote Sensing AI · GitHub
headline: RSandAI GitHub: GeoAI Research Outputs from Istanbul Technical University and Beyond
tldr: The RSandAI GitHub page hosts a collection of remote sensing and AI research outputs supervised by Prof. Dr. Elif SERTEL at Istanbul Technical University. It includes datasets, code, and results that showcase state‑of‑the‑art GeoAI techniques.
significance: It provides an open, reproducible resource for researchers and practitioners to advance GeoAI applications.

title: remote-sensing · GitHub Topics · GitHub
headline: Remote Sensing Change Detection: A Curated Collection of Datasets, Tools, and Competitions
tldr: This repository compiles the latest datasets, tools, methods, review papers, and competitions for remote sensing change detection. It serves as a go-to resource for researchers and practitioners to stay updated and benchmark their models.
significance: It accelerates research by centralizing high-quality resources, enabling faster development and evaluation of change detection algorithms.

title: RuView Free AI WiFi Sensing, ESP32 CSI Radar & Spatial Intelligence
headline: RuView: Open-Source AI WiFi Sensing with ESP32 CSI Radar for Spatial Intelligence
tldr: RuView is an open‑source, edge‑native AI WiFi sensing platform that transforms everyday ESP32 microcontrollers into long‑range spatial radar arrays. By converting ambient high‑frequency radio waves into detailed environmental telemetry, it enables real‑time spatial intelligence without cameras.
significance: RuView democratizes advanced radar sensing, making high‑resolution spatial awareness accessible on low‑cost hardware.

title: remote sensing free download - SourceForge
headline: Explore 38 Open-Source Remote Sensing Projects on SourceForge for Data Scientists
tldr: SourceForge hosts 38 open-source remote sensing projects, offering tools for building production-ready AI agents and models. Users can filter projects and access over 200 Google and third‑party AI models to accelerate development.
significance: These resources empower developers to rapidly prototype and deploy remote sensing solutions without licensing barriers.

title: Raster Vision: An open-source machine learning library for deep ...
headline: Raster Vision: Open-Source GIS and Deep Learning Pipeline for Satellite Image Analysis
tldr: Raster Vision is an open-source framework that unifies GIS and deep learning for remote sensing tasks. It offers configurable pipelines for chip classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection on satellite imagery.
significance: It empowers researchers and developers to build scalable, reproducible computer vision models for Earth observation without reinventing the wheel.

title: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
headline: Learning Task Models from Naturalistic Computer-Use Traces for Auditable AI Agents
tldr: By passively recording screenshots, mouse, and keyboard actions, we can derive symbolic models of everyday work. These models enable AI agents to learn real task flows and allow organizations to audit and reuse work knowledge.
significance: This approach bridges the gap between human workflow understanding and AI automation, ensuring transparency and reusability in workplace AI.

title: DreamHand: Repurposing Video Diffusion Models for Occlusion-Robust Egocentric 3D Hand Motion Recovery
headline: DreamHand: Recovering 3D Hand Motion from Occluded Egocentric Video Using Video Diffusion Models
tldr: DreamHand repurposes video diffusion models to robustly recover metric 3D hand trajectories from egocentric videos, even with severe occlusion and out-of-sight gaps. It achieves this by leveraging efficient inference techniques that avoid heavy, stochastic multi-step sampling.
significance: This approach enables scalable, accurate hand motion capture for embodied AI without requiring extensive labeled data or complex multi-view setups.

title: The Nearby Star Formation and Supernova Histories Reconstructed from Young Star Clusters
headline: Reconstructing Solar Neighborhood Star Formation and Supernova Histories Using Young Star Clusters
tldr: By integrating the past trajectories of Gaia-based young star clusters, we infer the recent star formation rate and core‑collapse supernova frequency in the Solar Neighborhood. The study links cluster ages, masses, and velocities to an axisymmetric Galactic potential to reconstruct a detailed time‑series of local stellar deaths.
significance: This work provides the first high‑resolution reconstruction of local star formation and supernova activity, offering a benchmark for Galactic evolution models.

title: Computational Methods of Wave Propagation for Semiclassical Models of High Harmonic Generation in Bulk Solids
headline: Self‑Consistent Maxwell–Bloch Simulation of High‑Order Harmonic Generation in Bulk Solids
tldr: We develop a self‑consistent computational framework that couples Maxwell’s equations with semiconductor Bloch equations to model nonlinear light‑matter interactions in bulk semiconductors. The method captures high‑order harmonic generation and its propagation, revealing distinct reflected and transmitted harmonic spectra.
significance: This approach provides a predictive tool for designing solid‑state high‑harmonic sources and understanding ultrafast light propagation in materials.

title: A two-point phase recovering with spherical wave reference
headline: Two-Point Phase Recovery Using Spherical Reference Waves in Helmholtz Exterior Problems
tldr: The paper presents two-point formulas to approximate the phase of a radiation solution by measuring the intensity of the combined total solution with a spherical reference wave. These formulas enable phase reconstruction in exterior Helmholtz problems without direct phase measurements.
significance: It offers a practical method for phase retrieval in wave propagation problems, aiding imaging and inverse scattering applications.

title: Zero-Sum Power Factor Games
headline: Zero-Sum Power Factor Games: Controlling Voltage with Reactive Power Pre-Selection
tldr: Operators can limit voltage deviations by remotely setting DER reactive power before active injections occur. This zero-sum game ensures constant power factor compliance per IEEE 1547-2018 while mitigating unpredictable active power fluctuations.
significance: It provides a proactive strategy to maintain grid stability amid volatile renewable generation.

title: A blind spot in transverse BAO calibration
headline: Blind Spot in Transverse BAO Calibration: Hidden Degeneracy with r_d h
tldr: Transverse BAO measurements rely on a calibration that cannot be constrained by cosmological data alone. A constant error in the BAO scale is degenerate with r_d h, making it invisible to standard analyses.
significance: This hidden degeneracy can bias cosmological parameter estimates, undermining the precision of BAO-based constraints.

title: Physical-Support Confidence Sets for Highly Coherent Dictionaries
headline: Resolving Physical Support Conflicts in Highly Coherent Dictionaries for Sparse Pursuit
tldr: We introduce a resolution-aware method that constructs confidence sets for the physical support of dictionary atoms, even when the dictionary is highly coherent. This approach reconciles calibration inconsistencies and yields more reliable interpretations in sparse pursuit applications.
significance: By providing statistically grounded support confidence sets, the method improves the interpretability and robustness of dictionary-based signal recovery in noisy, highly coherent settings.

title: QED radiative effects in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering: traditional and factorized approaches
headline: Comparing Traditional and Factorized QED Radiative Corrections for SIDIS Nucleon Structure
tldr: This study compares traditional and factorized approaches to QED radiative corrections in semi‑inclusive deep‑inelastic scattering. The authors find that the factorized method provides a more accurate extraction of parton distributions, especially at low transverse momentum.
significance: Accurate treatment of QED radiation is essential for precise determination of parton distribution functions from SIDIS experiments.

title: Non-Minimally Coupled Warm Inflation in the Defining Frame
headline: Warm Inflation Dynamics in F(Φ)R Theories: Defining vs Einstein Frame Analysis
tldr: We study warm inflation in scalar‑tensor F(Φ)R gravity in the defining frame and translate the dynamics to the Einstein frame. The dissipation ratio is reduced by modified‑gravity effects, showing that the effective warm‑inflation behavior can be consistently described in either frame.
significance: This work clarifies how modified gravity influences dissipation during warm inflation, aiding the interpretation of early‑universe models.

title: Programmable cavity QED with a fiber-integrated atomic array
headline: Fiber-Integrated Tweezer Array Enables Programmable Cavity QED with Rubidium Atoms
tldr: Researchers integrated a twelve‑site ^87Rb optical tweezer array into a high‑cooperativity fiber cavity, achieving strong, site‑resolved atom‑photon coupling. This platform opens pathways for scalable quantum networks and programmable quantum optics experiments.
significance: It demonstrates a scalable, controllable interface between neutral atoms and cavity QED, bridging tweezer arrays and high‑cooperativity cavities.

title: Group-theoretic treatment of strong light-matter coupling with an arbitrary number of excitations
headline: Group-Theoretic Approach to Multi-Excitation Strong Light-Matter Coupling
tldr: The paper extends polariton theory beyond single-excitation limits by employing group-theoretic methods, enabling accurate modeling of many-excitation dynamics. This framework paves the way for exploring complex light-matter phenomena in microcavities.
significance: It provides a powerful mathematical tool to capture multi-excitation physics, crucial for designing next-generation photonic devices.

title: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Patient-Oriented Medical Report Interpretation
headline: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Personalized Medical Report Interpretation
tldr: We present G-CARL, a framework that aligns reward learning with evidence-based checklists to generate patient-friendly interpretations of medical reports. The approach combines foundation model capabilities with grounded factuality and context-aware communication, addressing gaps in current vision-language tasks.
significance: G-CARL advances patient-centered care by ensuring medical reports are both factually accurate and easily understood by patients.

title: Large Sample Properties of Higher Order Markov Models
headline: Central Limit Theorem for Growing-Order Markov Chains on Finite Alphabets
tldr: We prove a central limit theorem for additive functionals of Markov chains whose order grows with sample size. The result uses return-time decompositions and requires mild ergodicity and sparsity conditions.
significance: The work extends classical Markov chain asymptotics to high-order models, enabling rigorous inference for complex time-series data.

title: An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
headline: Agentic Workflow Combines Chatbot Data Collection and Predictive Modeling for Travel
tldr: This study introduces a three-agent system that merges conversational data gathering, structured data processing, and behavior prediction for travel mode choices. A chatbot-administered, image-augmented survey demonstrates its effectiveness in real-world data collection.
significance: By integrating data collection and modeling, the approach reduces evaluation gaps and enhances predictive accuracy in travel behavior research.

title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
headline: AI4AI-Bench: Evaluating LLM Agents for Recursive Self-Improvement in Algorithmic Design
tldr: Recursive self‑improvement asks whether an AI can enhance the training algorithm that creates future AIs, thereby improving the compute‑capability exchange rate. AI4AI‑Bench tests LLM agents on this process, measuring how better objectives or update rules propagate across successive runs.
significance: Benchmarking RSI in LLM agents provides a systematic way to assess whether training improvements can be self‑propagated, informing safe and efficient AI evolution.
